## 2026-11-27 - ECurves: Extrude face
Asked: add extrude face to ECurves. Done: a picked face's menu (and E) - Extrude face: the face pulled out along its normal (the mouse along the normal's line, or a typed number; minus pushes it in), shown as a preview; click / Enter applies, Esc cancels. Walls of quads from the old rim to the new, rows about as tall as the face's quads are wide (1-64); the face's edges copied at the new rim (curves offset along the normal) and a straight side edge up each corner (where two of the face's edges meet), so the solid stays made of its edges; one undo step. Static face_extruded (part space) builds the mesh, fv and the new chains. Normal from the face's triangles the way Godot winds them (outwards). Test: test_extrude_face (a baked 1 m block's top pulled up 0.5 m: closed, top at 1.5, >=5 new edges, volume ~1.5, >=80% quads, undo).
Files: scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd, tests/test_curve_modeling.gd.

## 2026-11-27 - ECurves: a topology scorer and a baseline bench
Asked: a way to measure how well ECurves' meshes follow the topology rules (editor.md, mesh-curves-topology), and a baseline on the player character, before improving the layout. Done: topo_score.gd - score(v, t, fv, chains) pairs the triangles into faces (edge_net._pair_faces) and measures quads / triangles, poles (inner points where other than 4 faces meet; a valence histogram), quad shape (mean |corner - 90 deg|, mean aspect, slivers: aspect > 3 or a corner < 30 deg), size evenness (CV of face areas), shading (sides inside the faces whose triangles bend over 20 deg), open and non-manifold sides, and a 0..100 score (30 good quads, 20 poles, 15 square corners, 10 no slivers, 10 even sizes, 10 smooth shading, 5 manifold). ~90 ms for 10k triangles. tools/topo_bench.gd scores every "edges" solid of a model as it is and as edge_net.grid_any lays it out (timed), into a JSON report and a table. Baseline (the player, 91 solids, 144k triangles): as stored 66% quads, 12.9k poles, 51% slivers, 10.5% creased inner sides, mean score 32.7; grid_any 68% quads, 41.8k poles, 53% slivers, 16% creased, 29.4, no failures, 33 s in all (363 ms a solid, the Body 3 s). Test: test_topo_score (a regular grid ~100, flipped/jittered lower, a fan low, 9.8k triangles in under a second).
Files: scripts/editor/mesh/topo_score.gd, tools/topo_bench.gd, tests/test_topo_score.gd.

## 2026-11-27 - ECurves topology, step 1: the rules, a scorer, and a better layout (in progress)
Asked: a big improvement in ECurves' quad generation - clean quad topology that defines the edges, few triangles and distortions, smooth shading, easy to edit, following the edges' flow, grid-like quads; research good topology (a human face as the model; the user's guides: topologyguides.com, renderhub, elementza, cgcookie), write universal rules, always follow them; test on the player model; step by step.
Done so far:
- The rules: data/docs/editor.md "mesh-curves-topology" (edges are the frame; quads in grids; few poles, in quiet places, none of 6+; flow follows the edges; even and square; faces that don't fit are split, not forced; smooth shading).
- A scorer (scripts/editor/mesh/topo_score.gd: quads, poles, slivers, corner squareness, evenness, shading creases, manifold; 0-100) + tools/topo_bench.gd (a model's every solid: as stored vs laid out again, per-face layout log) + tests/test_topo_score.gd.
- The layout (edge_net.gd):
  - n-sided faces (3, 5, 6 corners) as n grids round ONE pole (Tarini's closed form for the spokes, cc_spokes / _face_cc) - the template artists use;
  - each face's corners planned (_plan_corners): its sharp corners, virtual ones added or sharp ones left on a side when that gives fewer poles / squarer quads; four-corner plans worked out exactly (opposite corners half way round); scored by how square the quads come out on the real rim lengths; round domes keep rings round a middle grid;
  - faces mapped flat with their real proportions (_flat_polygon, a proportioned rectangle for grids) and cotangent weights (_harmonic_cot, converging on long thin faces) - a plain average warped uneven triangulations into dented quads;
  - rim points placed by distance along the rim (_rim_places) - nearest-stretch guesses left coarse faces' ends unmapped;
  - an edge's sharp bends always mesh points; quads split along a diagonal inside them (a dented quad's longer diagonal turned a triangle over);
  - grid_faces face by face: a face that can't be gridded kept as it was, its rim's points kept so neighbours meet it (grid_faces_best); faces' facing made one way (oriented) and faces with holes cut into two pieces by internal lines (cut_holes, grid_any);
  - counts kept true to each edge's length (no inflating short sides to balance faces - the plans absorb it), thin strips accepted;
  - triangle pairing (_pair_faces) best first by quad squareness, true diagonals first, only real edge sides excluded - it lost many quads before (all ECurves meshes).
- Player model (91 solids), score 0-100: as stored 34.3; laid out again: 29.4 at the start -> 37.9 now; poles 43.7k -> 18.1k, slivers 55k -> 30k, shading creases 62k -> 35k; 0.35 s a solid (was 0.9).
- Tests: tests/test_topology.gd (triangle / pentagon / hexagon one pole or none, dome rings, thin band one strip), all 352 pass.
- Tried and backed out (recorded in code): Phong rounding of new points (more creases while the rim stays on the facets), bare open borders as edges (they're mostly seams in these meshes).
Next: the still-worse solids (Pauldron Red, Shin Red...), poles from rings/kept faces, the open-side seams, a band's end quads, then the bake/convert/settle paths using it, then the user's Head Armor.
Files: scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd, scripts/editor/mesh/topo_score.gd (new), tools/topo_bench.gd (new), tests/test_topology.gd (new), tests/test_topo_score.gd (new), data/docs/editor.md.
- (later the same day) Ring layouts used only on round faces (domes, discs): a long or many-cornered face whose plan fails keeps its own triangles instead of being wound round a circle; thin strips (a grid 1-3 quads wide) are never rejected as too coarse; points no triangle uses dropped from the edges before the layout (clean_edge_points). Player model now: 38.0 (stored 34.3), poles 15.2k (stored 13.0k), slivers 27.1k (stored 28.1k), shading creases 31.9k (stored 21.0k), 0.37 s a solid. Measured per layout: plain grids 33% slivers, one-pole layouts 30%, rings 16%. Faces still kept as they were: 274 - 151 an edge listing stray points off its path, 79 closed shapes with no edges, the rest odd cases. Tried and switched off: cutting closed edgeless shapes in two (split_closed - fewer slivers, more non-manifold sides), dropping run-breaking edge points (broke more than it mended).
- (step 2, 2026-11-27) More of the layout made robust, each measured on the player model and kept only if it helped:
  - each edge's points rebuilt as the path it really runs through the mesh (chain_paths: the mesh sides joining its points walked, along an open rim or a sharp bend first at a fork, its places by length again; strays dropped) - old edits had left edges whose listed points, in place order, made sides that aren't there, so they didn't cut the surface into faces;
  - the mesh's sharp bends that aren't edges (over 35 degrees, lines 3+ sides) made layout edges (crease_chains, let go of after) - rows lie exactly on them instead of folds and lumps (37.1 -> 39.0);
  - rounding new points onto the smooth surface (Phong; the rim's samples too, only where a triangle's normals agree within 35 degrees) - great on clean shapes (a coarse dome 83.6 -> 93.5), a small gain on the player;
  - the two-rim (annulus) layout places each rim loop as a whole, by length;
  - folded-quad and per-layout quality measured in the bench (tools/topo_bench.gd takes switches: -- <glb> <json> <filter|-> name=value...).
  - tried and off: plain-average map where cotangents fold, cutting lopsided rings in two, cutting closed edgeless shapes in two.
  Player model: 40.3 (stored 34.3; at the start of the work 29.4). tests/test_topology.gd: + a U-section ring band.
- (step 3, 2026-11-27) Remesh: a solid's menu (and the view's right-click menu) - the solid laid out again by the topology rules (grid_any) on a worker, one undo step (curve_tools.remesh_solid / _remesh_step; test_remesh_solid). Bakes use grid_any (its facing, folds, holes, kept faces) instead of the bare grid_faces. Creases: no minimum length (best on the player and the helmet); splitting big faces in two (split_big) tried - worse, off (big_face = 0). The user's Head Armor remeshed live after each step (60% quads, 28.6). Next: a field-aligned fill (Instant-Meshes-style, scripts/editor/mesh/field_remesh.gd - being written) for the faces the patch templates can't do (big organic faces like the helmet's).

## 2026-11-27 - ECurves topology, step 4: a field-aligned fill for big organic faces
Asked: a separate module (edge_net.gd calls it - not wired in yet) that lays out ONE face as field-aligned quads, in the spirit of Instant Field-Aligned Meshes (Jakob, Tarini, Panozzo, Sorkine-Hornung 2015), for the faces the patch templates can't do (the helmet's one big curved face with holes, few corners) - those were kept as their messy triangles. Its rim must be exactly the samples edge_net already placed (neighbours meet with no gap).
Done: scripts/editor/mesh/field_remesh.gd - fill_face(v, t, tris, loops, L) -> {pts, faces} ({} + `why` if it can't; validate() checks every result: rim samples all used, each rim side on one face, inner sides on two running opposite ways, nothing degenerate or facing away). Pure, static, worker-safe.
- Helper mesh: the face's triangles (flaps folded back on themselves cancelled out), the samples put into the rim and the rim's other points taken out (their triangles re-laid between the samples either side - the best of a family of fans - or the point pushed inside), remeshed evenly (sides ~0.55 L, longest-first splits in rounds, collapses, flips, smoothing); points found on the face along its normal (nearest-point projection piled points on a bent surface's corners and never ended); every change taken only when it makes nothing worse - a messy face's folds and slivers (the helmet's face starts with 251 of them) don't block it; folds untangled after.
- Fields on a hierarchy of graphs (pairs matched per level): a 4-RoSy orientation field held to the rim's tangent, then a position field (lattice of spacing L, rim samples fixed lattice points), Gauss-Seidel coarse to fine.
- Extraction: neighbours on the same lattice point collapsed (valid collapses only - stays a manifold with the same rim), moved onto it; triangles paired into quads (greedy by quality + augmenting paths); pole pairs undone (a quad whose opposite inner corners merge when that leaves fewer poles: +6 to +10 score points); a squaring relaxation on the surface.
Numbers (topo_score 0-100; the face's own triangles in brackets): dome 86.6 (81.9) 95% quads 30 poles; six-sided face with a hole 77.5 (86.1) 90% quads; coarse U band 83.9 (67.0) 98% quads; ribbon 100; a 4032-triangle dome 91.7 (89.8) in 1.6 s; the user's Head Armor's biggest face (3690 triangles, 8 rims, L 0.0106): 78.2 (28.7), 93% quads (60%), poles 103 of 1034 inner points (753 of 1594), slivers 7 (526), 4.0 s headless.
Weak spots: ~5% triangles left (at the field's singularities, where the rim's spacing doesn't match the lattice); a few pole pairs; a face much smaller than L comes out as a couple of quads and triangles; a badly folded input (more than ~5% triangles turned over) can fail its own check and give {} (the caller keeps the face as it was); the helper mesh's density makes a fine face (small L) the slow case (~4 s for the helmet's face).
Files: scripts/editor/mesh/field_remesh.gd (new), tests/test_field_remesh.gd (new: dome, hexagon with a hole, curved band, messy face, rim given the other way round, rim samples kept, a 4000-triangle face under 5 s).
- (step 4 wired in, 2026-11-27) The field-aligned fill now runs inside the layout: grid_faces_best settles every face the templates can do, then lays out the faces it had to keep (odd counts round them, big organic faces) with field_remesh on their own rim points (fill_face(..., own_rim = true): no resampling, so neighbours meet them exactly); a rim pinched at a point (two fans of triangles touching only there) split into a copy a fan first (HM._unpinch). The user's Head Armor (copy): 29.6 -> 47.1, quads 61% -> 70%, poles 757 -> 288, slivers 579 -> 133, shading creases 709 -> 409; 19 of its 20 kept faces filled (the 3585-triangle main face included), ~10 s headless. Live on the user's Head Armor: 4251 -> 3238 triangles, 69% quads, score 45.5.
- (step 5, 2026-11-27) The fill made dependable and given every face a chance:
  - kept faces' rims resampled like any other face's (the fill gets those samples: field_remesh.fill_face(..., own_rim, {keep, split}) puts them into the face's own rim and takes its other points out) - a face it can't do that way is filled on its own points next round (fill_fixed); grids made first, fills last; fills cached between rounds;
  - each face laid out both ways - the grid templates and the field-aligned fill - and the better kept by its own topo_score (fill_compare; edge_net._fill_wins / _local_score): a flat twelve-cornered cross 64.1 -> 100, the player's Hand L Armor 16.6 -> 83.2, Fingers L Armor 15.7 -> 77.1;
  - the fill no longer gives up a whole face for a few folded quads (up to 1 in 200 kept), its refining capped (a badly folded face split on and on - 770k triangles, a hang), a rim pinched at a point split per fan, a thin place's cross side split so a rim point can come out;
  - small faces it can't fill (a ring of a few triangles) cut into triangles across their rim samples (ears in their plane, holes bridged in);
  - crease lines (crease_chains) measured again with the fill: on the Head Armor they cut tiny loops round single triangles that nothing lays out (49.0 with them, 69.5 without).
  Head Armor (copy): 69.5, 87% quads, poles 143, slivers 21 (stored 28.2; 61%, 757 poles, 579 slivers).
  Player model (91 solids) with each face's better layout: 74.4 with crease lines, 71.8 without (stored 34.3; 40.3 before this step) - quads 89.7%, poles 9.7k (stored 13.0k), slivers 4.9k (stored 28.1k), shading creases 21.9k (stored 21.0k); ~5.7 s a solid headless (on a worker). Crease loops shorter than 6 quads dropped (crease_loop_min). Live on the user's Head Armor (from its original triangles): 4626 -> 2568 triangles, 88% quads, 71.9.
  Tests: test_topology.test_cross_laid_out_by_its_flow (a twelve-cornered cross: all quads, closed, open only round its rim).
- (step 6, 2026-11-27) Crease lines tried both ways per solid: laid out with crease lines of 4+ quads and with only those of 8+ (closed ones under 6 quads never), the better by topo_score kept (grid_any's crease_both; lengths passed as arguments - no statics changed on a worker). Player model: creases 4+ 74.8, 8+ 72.7 (Head Armor the other way round: 62.1 / 70.1).
  Player model with both tried: 75.2 (quads 90.7%, poles 9.1k, slivers 7.1k, shading creases 24.1k; ~12 s a solid on a worker).
  A bake no longer runs the full layout on the main thread (seconds now): it lays the solid out with the grid templates only (grid_any(..., full = false), a fraction of a second), then the full layout - fill and all - follows on a worker once any joining is done (remesh_after -> remesh_solid, its own undo step "Lay out (the bake's topology)"); a remesh whose solid was edited meanwhile isn't put in. Tests: test_bake_lays_out_in_background; the remesh test waits by time. All 363 tests pass.
  Files: scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd, scripts/editor/mesh/field_remesh.gd, scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd, tests/test_topology.gd, tests/test_curve_modeling.gd, tools/topo_bench.gd, data/docs/editor.md.
- (step 7, 2026-11-27) The topology rules everywhere a mesh is made:
  - conversion: a solid whose edges aren't on its points (the even-mesh fallback) laid out by the full layout on its worker (the usual conversion keeps the model's own triangles exactly, quadified, as before);
  - knife: the faces either side of a cut laid out again in the background - only those (grid_any's `only`: triangles to lay out; every other face frozen - its triangles and its edges' points exactly as they were, never filled) - its own undo step "Lay out (the knife's faces)";
  - settling after an edit: the faces at the edges it moved laid out again the same way in the background, put into the edit's own undo step (no extra step) - solids made of a model's own triangles (dense) excepted, as their regridding already was.
  - the fill ~2x faster: helper mesh sides 0.85 L (was 0.55), fewer smoothing sweeps - no loss measured (Hand L Armor 84.4 -> 86.3); up to 3% folded quads tolerated (the comparison decides).
  Tests: test_knife_faces_laid_out_again, test_settle_lays_moved_faces_out; all 365 pass.
  Player model with the faster fill: 75.7 (quads 91.3%, poles 8.7k, slivers 7.0k), 6.3 s a solid headless (was 12.1). Shading creases per inner side: 7.1% (stored meshes 10.5%) - the raw count is higher only because the new meshes have more sides. User's Head Armor (live, from its original triangles): 2568 triangles, 88% quads, 71.9.
  Docs: data/docs/editor.md "mesh-curves-topology" - the flow layout, the bake/knife/edit background layouts.
- (2026-11-27) Asked: a progress bar while remeshing, in the view's lower left corner. Done: the layout reports how far it's got and what it's doing (EdgeNet.progress, never going back: the two crease tries each half, the grids a quarter of each, then its faces weighted by triangles - the big faces are the slow ones); while a remesh / a bake's, knife's or edit's background layout runs, a panel in the view's lower left corner shows the solid, the percentage, the stage and a bar (curve_tools._remesh_bar), gone when it's done. test_remesh_solid checks it's there and goes.
- (2026-11-27) Remesh in the right-click menu whatever's picked: with a face picked (beside Face finer / Extrude face / Face coarser) and with the whole solid picked, not only with the solid selected and nothing picked (curve_tools._remesh_of, _patch_part; test_remesh_in_every_solid_menu).
- (2026-11-27) Asked: "if it's subdivide why not call it subdivide?" - Face finer / Face coarser renamed Subdivide face / Unsubdivide face (menu, undo steps, messages), the panel's Face resolution now Face subdivisions; their tooltips and the guide say it adds points without changing the layout (Remesh lays it out again, replacing the subdivisions). The old names kept as the guide section's search keywords.

## 2026-11-27 - ECurves: Save writes over the opened file; Save as with a full file browser
Asked: "save or save as should overwrite the existing file if the model is loaded from that file, also i need a full save dialog with the relevant file browser as you would expect in blender, use blender as an example of how save and save as behavior should work".
Done:
- Save writes over the file the model was opened from - its own file, or the open variant's (it no longer makes a new variant when the original is open: mesh_editor._write_target); a never-saved model asks where (Save as). Saved over an original that has variants: it says the game still uses the latest (Revert to original to use it). In a mod: the mod's copy as before.
- The game shows an overwritten model at once: a model file newer than its import is read as glTF at run time till it's imported again (ModelOverride.stale - characters through Stage3D).
- Save as: a file browser (scripts/ui/file_browser.gd, FileBrowser.open(owner, {title, action, dir, file, filters, thumb, done, cancel})) - places (the game, Models, Art, Overrides, home, desktop, documents, downloads) and Recent folders (user://file_browser.json); Back / Forward (Alt+Left/Right), Parent (Backspace), Refresh, New folder (named inline); the path (typed: go there); Search; only .glb/.gltf or every file; list (name, date modified, size - sorted by a click on a column's title, again reversed) or thumbnails (the model browser's turning pictures); click a file - its name, double-click - a folder in / a file saved over; the file name with -/+ (Ctrl+Minus/Plus: the number at its end down/up), Cancel (Esc), Save As (Enter); a name that's there shows red ("overwrites it"). Anywhere on disk: inside the game's folder saved as res://, else the absolute file; the file saved as is the model's from then on. A new model's name: untitled.glb.
- Tooltips (Save as, Revert to original) and the guide's "mesh-save" section rewritten.
- Tests: test_save_overwrites_the_opened_file (a scratch file outside the game), test_save_as_browser; test_save_is_an_override_with_variants now saves into a variant (never the game's own file).
Files: scripts/ui/file_browser.gd (new), scripts/editor/mesh_editor.gd, scripts/world/models/model_override.gd, tests/test_mesh_editor.gd, data/docs/editor.md.

## 2026-11-27 - Fix: a remesh crash (laying some faces out again)

- Asked: the game crashed during play (a Remesh / background layout in the ECurves editor).
- Cause: edge_net.grid_faces - a frozen face (kept as it was in a partial layout: knife, edit, `only`) took
  `out_v = fill_out_v` though no fill had run for it - the static still held an earlier face's (or an earlier
  solid's) shorter point list, so the next faces indexed past its end ("Invalid access of index 172").
  Now only a fill that actually ran hands its points over.
- Also: a fill that lost to the grid (_fill_wins) rolled back its rim points (new_of) but not the places it
  had given them on the edges (fv_out / fv_seen) - those named points that weren't there, or other points
  later. Rolled back too.
- Test: test_topology.test_part_laid_out_again_keeps_the_rest (a partial layout with stale leftovers: every
  corner and every edge point valid).
- Files: scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd, tests/test_topology.gd.

## 2026-11-27 - Fix: a knife cut that stops inside a face floated off the mesh

- Asked: "when i use the knife the resulting curve seems to be disconnected from the underlying solid".
- Cause: the layout (Remesh, and the knife's own background layout of the faces beside the cut) splits a
  solid into faces at its edges - an edge that runs into a face and stops there (a knife cut not crossing it
  from side to side) splits nothing, so the face was laid out from its rim alone and the cut's points were
  left in no triangle: the curve drawn over the surface, moving it moved nothing.
- Fix: edge_net.grid_faces - such a face ("slit": an edge's side with the face's triangles on both sides) is
  kept as it was, the edge's points with it (frozen; its inner edge sides kept as kept_edges).
- Test: test_curve_modeling.test_knife_cut_ending_inside_a_face_stays_in_the_mesh (fails without the fix:
  9 loose points, 8 gaps).
- Files: scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd, tests/test_curve_modeling.gd.
